A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MGFR research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, with retained content identifiable across additions and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original face-restoration experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations and a user study in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, computational measurements, an adapter ablation and a qualitative seed-stability illustration.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the architecture, two-stage training and classifier-free guidance procedure. New Appendix J outlines a limited video inference adaptation using the restored previous frame as the current frame's reference. It reports neither a new temporal module nor a video evaluation.

E1.justification: The evaluated coverage remains FFHQ/Reface-HQ training, CelebA-Test, Reface-Test and real-world images including WebPhoto-Test. Revised dataset counts concern sample sizes and splits, without a documented change in represented domains. Appendix J discusses video applicability but reports no video experiment.

E2.justification: v2 adds BFRffusion to the CelebA-Test comparisons in Tables 1 and 9–11, SUPIR to qualitative comparisons on CelebA-Test and Reface-Test in Figures 30–31, and both methods to Table 12's resource comparison. These extend the existing comparator sets without replacing the established comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported Reface-HQ totals change from 23,500 images/5,250 identities to 21,500/4,800; training identities change from 4,870 to 4,520, and Reface-Test changes from 1,800 images/380 identities to 1,300/280. These are reported setting revisions, without evidence that experiments were rerun. v2 also adds parameter-count/FLOPs evaluation and a single-adapter control; Appendix L merely explains existing quality metrics.

E4.justification: Figure 32 adds a single-versus-dual-control-adapter ablation, illustrating poorer recovery and color inconsistency with the single adapter. Figure 29 adds a one-input seed-stability illustration. These are limited supplementary analyses; the existing prompt, identity, information-flow, training-volume and sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix K newly presents outputs labeled with six inference seeds: 2982, 78, 11281, 15, 424 and 9168. This adds qualitative seed reporting, but neither aggregate repeated-run statistics nor confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. It does not establish additional training runs.

E6.justification: Existing restoration scores are retained, while v2 adds BFRffusion scores, SUPIR examples, resource measurements and qualitative ablation/stability findings. Some numerical rankings change: at ×16, BFRffusion's LPIPS of 0.3735 is lower than MGFR's retained 0.3760. These are additional comparison results, not demonstrated performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The embedding definitions and guidance equation (1) are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and the added metric overview gives explanatory descriptions rather than new mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the stated dataset contribution from over 23,000 images and 5,000 identities to over 21,000 images and 4,800 identities. The principal restoration, multimodal guidance and novelty claims remain; the 'first multi-modal' claim already appeared in v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: Appendix D corrects the efficiency interpretation from marginal improvement over DiffBIR to higher time/memory cost, and adds explanations of single-adapter failures and possible compression. Appendix J discusses temporal consistency and video applicability. Section 4.5 removes the explicit caveat that high-quality references may be unavailable and states the benefit of multiple references more definitively.

D1.justification: Table 12 newly discloses parameter counts and FLOPs, including MGFR's 2,029.3 million parameters and 890.5/2,672.4 GFLOPs without/with guidance. These are additional technical disclosures, not evidence of resized models. The optimizer, hardware, training durations, prompt-processing details and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds cited works including Chen et al. (2024), Li et al.'s multi-scale component dictionaries (2020a), and Teng et al. (2022). It also develops comparisons with the already-cited SUPIR work. The main related-work organization and novelty positioning remain, while duplicate bibliographic entries do not constitute additional distinct works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and citation-format edits, rewrites parts of the limitations and efficiency discussions, and adds Appendices J–M with a metric overview. It also updates affiliations/publication headers and adds an acknowledgment. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 29–32, expands comparison-table rows and adds parameter/FLOPs columns to Table 12. Existing appendix figures move with text reflow, while most earlier displays remain. Some ranking colors are inconsistent with the added scores, notably the retained best-LPIPS highlighting for MGFR at ×16.

improvement.justification: Additional baseline comparisons, the direct adapter ablation and model-complexity reporting modestly strengthen empirical support and transparency. Appendix D also corrects v1's erroneous efficiency interpretation. These benefits are limited by unexplained dataset-size revisions despite retained scores, single-example stability evidence, unevaluated video claims and ranking highlights that do not consistently reflect the new baseline results.
